anomalies.observed: R10 and R11 are 2.2k 1% resistors in series with the USB data lines.
anomalies.expected: USB 2.0 series resistors should be approximately 22Ω (e.g., 22Ω or 27Ω) for impedance matching; 2.2kΩ is about 100× too high and will severely attenuate USB signals.
anomalies.impact: USB communication on the affected ports will likely fail or be highly unreliable due to excessive series resistance.

anomalies.observed: R17 is drawn with a resistor reference prefix (R) but has a capacitor value of 22pF, placed in the feedback network of the boost converter U12.
anomalies.expected: A feedback feedforward capacitor in this location should be a capacitor, e.g., C17 22pF; a resistor with a 22pF value is inconsistent with the part type and function.
anomalies.impact: If a resistor is fitted, the boost converter feedback network is incorrect and may oscillate or regulate poorly; if a capacitor is fitted, the BOM/reference designation is wrong.

anomalies.observed: The logic-side ground (GND1, pin 4) and bus-side ground (GND2, pin 5) of the isolated CAN transceivers U11 and U10 are both connected to the same GND net.
anomalies.expected: For an isolated CAN transceiver, GND1 and GND2 must be separate isolated grounds to maintain galvanic isolation between the logic side and the CAN bus side.

evidence.quote: U11 GND1 pin 4 to GND; U11 GND2 pin 5 to GND
two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (U8, U9) through an isolated CAN transceiver (U11/companion)

anomalies.impact: The intended galvanic isolation between the logic ground and CAN bus ground is defeated, removing protection against ground loops and common-mode noise.

The USB resistor error is the most clearly supported and likely to cause USB failure.
